snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹40 lakh–1.5 crore for a wide size range, your own moulds and retail presence
snapshot.margin_d2c: 55–65% gross margin on your own site, before returns and ads
snapshot.distribution_note: Instagram and marketplaces work; size-related returns are the main cost

tailwinds: Agra, Kanpur, Chennai-Ambur and Kolkata are major footwear clusters that make small runs for new brands.
Comfort, orthopaedic and sneaker categories are growing fast as buyers spend more on their feet.
BIS quality rules now apply to much footwear, pushing out the cheapest low-quality imports.
Sneaker culture has turned shoes into a fashion and collecting category for young buyers.
headwinds: Footwear needs many sizes per design, so stock ties up a lot of cash.
Returns for fit often run at 20–30% online.
Bata, Campus, Puma and marketplace labels are strong at every price point.
Mould and last costs make every new design expensive to develop.
angle_2026: Footwear quality rules have pushed out the cheapest imports, and buyers are paying more for comfort. In 2026, the footwear brands that grow own a clear need, such as orthopaedic support, work shoes for standing jobs or sneakers with a design identity, and solve fit with better size guides and exchanges.
cost_basis: Estimated for a brand using a contract manufacturer in a footwear cluster, launching 4–6 designs across sizes, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Design, sample pairs, sole moulds if custom

unit_economics.example: For a ₹2,499 pair sold on your own site:
rows: ₹300–600 per pair after ads and returns
unit_economics.note: Exchanges instead of refunds, half sizes where possible and honest size charts cut returns more than anything else.

investor_probes: What is your return rate, and how much is due to size?
How many sizes and colours are sitting unsold?
What does each first order cost in ads?
Why would a buyer choose you over Campus or a marketplace label?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start with 2–3 designs in your core sizes, sell pre-orders or small batches, and reorder only what sells. Add half sizes and wider fits once you know demand.
sourcing_edge: Agra and Kanpur (leather and casual shoes), Ambur and Chennai (leather and export shoes), Kolkata and Delhi's Bahadurgarh (sports and PU shoes) will take small orders. Direct relationships with a factory owner get you better prices and priority.
licences: BIS certification under the footwear quality control orders, where it applies to your product
Correct labelling of material, size and maker details

hard_truths.title: Sizes lock up cash
hard_truths.text: Every design needs 6–10 sizes. A slow size can leave you with hundreds of pairs you can't sell at full price.

hard_truths.title: Returns
hard_truths.text: Fit problems drive returns, and each one costs two-way shipping. Invest in size charts, fit notes and easy exchanges.

hard_truths.title: Moulds are expensive
hard_truths.text: Custom soles need moulds that cost lakhs. Use existing sole designs from your manufacturer until you have proven demand.

hard_truths.title: Big brands own the price
hard_truths.text: Campus, Bata and marketplace labels sell good-enough shoes cheaply. You need a clear reason to exist beyond price.

plan_goal: The aim is 300 pairs sold with a return rate below 20%.

plan.title: Choose your niche
steps: Pick one buyer and one need, such as office comfort, orthopaedic support or sneakers.
Visit a footwear cluster and meet 3–5 manufacturers.

plan.title: First run
steps: Test samples on 20 people for a week each.
Produce a small run in your core sizes.
Register GST, Udyam and your trademark.

plan.title: Sell
steps: Launch on your own site and one marketplace.
Send pairs to 20 creators in your niche.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Check returns by size and design.
Decide on the next design or channel.
